Power 
 Stations | Technical Procedure
Introduction
This document lists the equipment inspection I1, which must be 
 performed 
 very 
 10 years as indicated by Y10 in the title block. or 
 10,000 no-load operations, or 5,000 on load operations, or 15 fault 
 interruptions
The 
 first draft initiated by eng. Mohamed Hessen Ebraheem 
 and tested by: eng.Nabeel Saad Ebraheem, at 31July2003. and accepted by general director eng. Shauky

 eng.Mohamed Mahdey Alnshar Head Sector of

Safety 
Precautions
A work permit 
 must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable 
 safety category,
Safety fence 
 (rope) with caution marks surrounding the work area,
Wear safety 
 helmet, shoes.
A work permit 
 must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable 
 safety category,
The breaker must be at first 
 in the opened and discharged status.
Tools and Equipment
Safety helmet.
A (2500 V) Megger
Work to be Carried Out
Electrical Checks
Insulation Tests
Primary Disconnects
A (2500 V) 
 Megger is used to measures the insulation resistance (phase to phase and 
 Phase to ground) a typical Value of the resistance is > 10000 Mega Ohm.
Secondary disconnects
Connect all the 
 secondary disconnect pins by a conducting wire except pin 24 (ground pin),
Measure the 
 insulation resistance by a 500 V Megger
Primary Circuit Resistance
Put the breaker in the closed position.
Use a low resistance measuring instrument (100 A) rated.
Resistance is measured between the breakers primary bars.
Breaker | Resistance 
 range (Micro Ohm)
1200 A | 30-60
2000 A | 25-50
3000 A | 5-25
Vacuum Interrupter Integrity Test
This test is required to ensure that no loss of vacuum occurred. It needs 
 a high voltage AC power source with variable gradual output.
Put 
 the breaker in the TRIP position.
A dry 
 cloth should very well clean the entire vacuum interrupter surface.
Apply 
 A 36 kV (rms) 50/60 Hz and 500 v/sec hold for 10 seconds.
No 
 breakdown should occur for the interrupter to pass this test.
If 
 a breakdown occurs at a voltage V1 then repeat the test, the 
 interrupter will be accepted if it passes the second test.
If the 
 breakdown occurs again at V2>V1 then stop the procedure, 
 remove the high voltage source, and Discharge any residual electric charge by 
 a grounded cable, then restart.
If the 
 breakdown occurs again at V2 = V1 then stop the 
 procedure, then the interrupter is said to fail passing the test.
If the 
 test failed for the third time, the vacuum is believed to be lost.
Remove 
 the high Ac Voltage source.
Discharge any residual electric charge by a grounded cable.
A 
DC source of 50 kV maximum for 10 seconds can be used but half way rectifier 
testers is not recommended for use.
